test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A train of length 120 m moving at 60 km/h crosses a 180-meter bridge in how many seconds?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = Train length + Bridge length

⇒ 120 + 180 = 300 m

60 km/h = 60 × 5 ÷ 18 = 50 ÷ 3 m/s

Time = 300 ÷ (50 ÷ 3) = 18 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 18 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train = 120 m

Length of bridge = 180 m

Speed of train = 60 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

 
• Train = 120 m 
• Bridge = 180 m Total Distance = 300 m 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance covered = 120 + 180 = 300 m

⇒ Speed = 60 × 5 ÷ 18 = 50 ÷ 3 m/s

⇒ Time = 300 ÷ (50 ÷ 3)

⇒ = 300 × 3 ÷ 50

⇒ = 18 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 18 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Train Crossing Bridge

Distance covered = Length of Train + Length of Bridge.

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h into m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18.

Train Crossing Pole

Distance covered equals only the train length when crossing a pole.

Relative Speed

For two moving trains, use relative speed instead of individual speed.
